decisions.summary: A record answer is counted as mixed only by an uncommitted file in RECORD: owed, bundle, their path dependencies (core, pool, registry, research, rust/guard/shared), rust/gate/src and the record crate; the record crate's other dependencies (archive, downloads, pages, semantic, trials, uncited) are left out on a grep of every caller of write_answer/write_judged.
decisions.why: This is the tooling_fix of ask:mixed-build-53-record-answers: an answer is mixed only when a dirty path lies in the closure of the crates that built and recorded it (owed, bundle and their transitive deps). RECORD is a superset of that closure. It adds rust/gate/src and the record crate, which keeps more of T197 than the ruling requires. The crates left out are not in the ruling's closure in the first place.

decisions.summary: A Markdown file outside the table's crates never counts; a Markdown file inside a table crate counts (include_str! fixtures).
decisions.why: The ruling names rust/gate/CLAUDE.md as a dirty path whose code could not have run. Markdown inside a table crate still counts, and the closure walk flags any included file the table does not count, so no file that can run is dropped.

decisions.summary: tests.rs and tests/ files inside a table crate still count; no test-only exclusion.
decisions.why: This counts more than the ruling's closure would strictly require, so T197 is kept. It is not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: Any Cargo.toml, rust/Cargo.lock and .cargo/config.toml always count, and so does a path the rule does not know.
decisions.why: This is conservative. It keeps T197's rule for every file whose effect on the build the closure cannot rule out.

decisions.summary: The claims side's mixed-build test is narrowed the same way through its own table CLAIMS (the claims crate's path-dependency closure, rust/gate/src, and the record crate's one included file), through the single Landing::paths call.
decisions.why: The tooling_fix names only the owed crate's record gate, so narrowing the claims side's T197 rule goes past its letter. The ruling's own why gives the reason. It calls the fault a false positive 'of the same class as mixed-build-241-claims', and it orders that the rule be narrowed by a tool and not waived again. Counting a dirty file that no claims verb can run is that same wrong outcome: a check refusing good work. Fixing it in this step is required by fix-as-we-go. The purpose test holds: T197 exists so that an answer judged by code that is not its own is not trusted. Code outside the claims verbs' closure cannot have judged the answer, and the closure test keeps the table honest as dependencies change.

decisions.summary: build::closure::gaps walks the [dependencies]/[build-dependencies] path entries and the include_str!/include_bytes! lines from each table's roots. It reports an unlisted crate that is reached, an entry nothing reaches, or an uncounted included file. Core's test runs it on the real tree, and core's Cargo.toml declares those crates so rust-test re-runs when a manifest moves.
decisions.why: This is the ruling's own requirement, 'a fixed table whose test fails when a dependency is added', and it only enforces that. Reading the include lines closes the rust/guard/shared to record-crate gap the plan found.

decisions.summary: The refusal message is unchanged. The fix is built before T218..T223 are re-landed, while nothing else records in the clone.
decisions.why: This follows the ruling's what (3) to (5) exactly.

decisions.summary: One reading type, Own, in core/build.rs; mixed asks it; Judged (owed/answers.rs) and Landing (claims/index.rs) each hold one Own in place of their own HEAD lookups
decisions.why: Where the fix lives, not what it trusts. The ruling's tooling_fix names both the owed record and the claim answers, and one shared reading puts the same rule in both.

decisions.summary: A stamped blob is the landing's own where it is its path's blob at HEAD, at a commit of the delta, or at the base; a stamped deleted is own where one of those commits holds no such file
decisions.why: This is the ruling's tooling_fix nearly word for word. The deleted arm is the same rule applied to a file's absence.

decisions.summary: Base = git merge-base HEAD origin/main (the base make land already diffs from); delta = base..HEAD; a merge of main moves the base and keeps the clone's own commits in the delta
decisions.why: The ruling names 'the landing's delta (f7c105b4a0..HEAD)' and 'its base' without saying how to find them. Using the landing's own diff base reads them as make land already does.

decisions.summary: Where no base is found (no origin/main, no shared history) the delta is empty and a blob is held to HEAD, the rule before this task ((d) still applies where the stamp commit is known)
decisions.why: With no base the ruling's delta and base are undefined, so the ruling's rule has nothing to compare against. The fallback is the stricter earlier rule: it trusts less, never more.

decisions.summary: A blob no commit holds still reads mixed (the real case: another builder's work in progress); measured over 302 record entries and 205 claim rows, one superseded answer holds such blobs
decisions.why: This keeps T197 unchanged. The ruling widens 'own' only to committed blobs, so an uncommitted blob still reads mixed, as it did before.

decisions.summary: A blob held at a commit of <stamp commit>..HEAD is also committed code, asked after HEAD/delta/base miss; a stamp commit git does not know adds nothing
decisions.why: This trusts more than the ruling's words, so it is tested as an exception. Taken literally, the ruling's rule would defeat the ruling's own stated purpose: 'ends the loop' and 'do not ask this question again'. The block measures it: once this landing is pushed, its commits fall behind the next landing's base. 189 claim rows stamped 1b064aa0de would then read mixed at the next landing of any clone, the same loop run once more. Against T197's purpose: (d) admits a blob only if a commit reachable from HEAD holds it, so it can never admit a blob that no commit holds. Another builder's uncommitted work therefore still reads mixed under (c). With (d), the block measures 0 of 205 rows and 0 of 302 record entries, the (c) one aside, left holding a blob that no commit since its stamp holds. It trusts only committed code, which is the ruling's own ground for its rule.

decisions.summary: build::current() drops from the stamp each dirty file whose stamped blob equals the launcher tree's HEAD now, so an answer by a binary whose sources were since committed unchanged carries a clean stamp and a triage clear by it writes no build row
decisions.why: The ruling's second clause is worded as a reading rule ('reads a stamp as clean once all its dirty blobs equal HEAD'). (f) applies it when the stamp is written, per file, against HEAD at that moment, which goes past the words, so it is tested as an exception. It is implied by the ruling's own clause, and it admits nothing T197 guards: a file is dropped only when its blob is committed at HEAD when the answer is recorded, so uncommitted work (T197's object) is never dropped and still reads mixed under (c). The one case where it differs from the read-time rule is a write-time HEAD the landing later loses through an amend or reset. That gives the answer the same standing a clean build at an amended-away commit already has, because the mixed rule reads only dirty blobs, so it opens no new class of trusted code. Without (f), the defect the block records goes on: each triage clear writes a build row into the tracked index for files that were HEAD's own. That is a wrong outcome the ruling's clause was aimed at.

decisions.summary: Built straight after the landing of T218-T224, alone in the clone, nothing recording answers while the gate's crates are uncommitted
decisions.why: The ruling's 'what' step (3): 'straight after the landing, alone in the clone'.

decisions.summary: Red-first fixtures in the owed and claims crates for an answer by a build of an earlier commit of the delta, plus opposite cases (blob no commit holds re-owed; unknown stamp commit with no base re-owed) and a core fixture per arm of Own
decisions.why: The ruling asks for 'a red fixture where an answer's stamped blob matches an earlier commit of the delta but not HEAD'. The opposite cases enforce T197, which is kept, so they are enforcement of what was asked, not extra scope.

decisions.summary: items::items reads a comment inside an item tag's token as part of it; items::faults names any item tag still unreadable, with the form to write.
decisions.why: A defect fix (a tool that answers wrongly: the owing, the backlog and the claims missed toe-shoulder-past-corner). decisions.summary: Only GUESS, UNRESEARCHED, DEVIATION and CONVENTION items owe; ATTESTED-type items do not owe a form unit.
decisions.why: Does not narrow anything asked: a moved Drawing: page still owes modal-depiction for every other change (modals::owed_row, unchanged). The four labels are the ones whose disclosure is the form check's job.

decisions.summary: A CONVENTION item also owes a modal-form unit, though the form contract leaves CONVENTION to modal-depiction.
decisions.why: Widens rather than narrows owing, and the triage bounds it; whether a form unit with nothing to judge is worth its cost is design, not fidelity. The rationale cites T236's line, which is not in this bundle and is not the GM's words; nothing here rests on it.

decisions.summary: A tag added to words that stood on the page before (T192's tagging) owes nothing.
decisions.why: Is the GM's own approved rules, not a carve-out from them: 2026-11-23 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review' and the T192 route ('a script tags each block that names its own label'). Adding a tag to words already there does not change a claim.

decisions.summary: A pop-up whose Guesses tab already references the item as {NNNN#id} is not owed; the bullet regenerates from the tag (T187).
decisions.why: Directly the GM's 2026-11-23 rule 'labels are data and propagate by regeneration' and his question 'Shouldn't attested versus guess be something that cascades mechanically rather than requiring a review'.

decisions.summary: A changed label on a drawing-page item owes the form check of a pop-up that does not reference the item.
decisions.why: Counted as an exception to 'labels ... propagate by regeneration' (GM 2026-11-23), so it was judged per case, starting from presumed illegitimate. (a) Where the pop-up references the item, the exemption above applies and regeneration carries it, which is the rule as written. (b) Where the pop-up does not reference the item, regeneration has nothing to act on, so the rule cannot apply there. The plan also records that the label word is held in the block's prose (items::faults), so a relabel is a claim change under the GM's 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review'. A relabel to GUESS or UNRESEARCHED also gives the pop-up a new duty under the 2026-11-25 rule the GM approved ('UNRESEARCHED a fifth label on the research pages as well as in the claims'). Where a relabel only exposes a gap that already stood (GUESS to UNRESEARCHED on an unreferenced item), the 2026-11-25 rule still applies, because it puts the new label in the claims. The exception does not empty the regeneration rule, which still covers every referenced item.

decisions.summary: Triage rule (D): a labeled figure of the pop-up's own thing that its Guesses tab does not hold is sent on; the plan names it the one exception to 'a gap filled is a completion, not a correction'.
decisions.why: Starting from presumed illegitimate, and testing both pairs. The GM's own words reach both, so this is not inference. P7: the pop-up says rows ran to 300 ft while the map draws none past 145 ft as a GUESS. A reader is misled, which is a factual finding of the kind the 2026-11-23 rules keep cascading ('only factual findings cascade'), not a style gap. P15: a new UNRESEARCHED toe-shoulder-past-corner that hamlet/marsh does not hold. Here the GM's approval of 2026-11-25 ('UNRESEARCHED a fifth label on the research pages as well as in the claims'; 'note it as being something that is unresearched') requires the label to reach the claims, so leaving it out breaks a rule he approved. The 2026-11-24 instruction ('we really are cascading in situations that do call for it') covers both cases. Purpose test: the gap-fill clause was dropped because completion edits fixed no real flaw. A drawn guess that the pop-up never discloses is the flaw the label rules exist to show, so applying the drop here would defeat their purpose. The scope is narrow: only new or relabeled items, and only of the pop-up's own kind ('An item about another kind on the same page is not (D)'). The cited dev/modals.md M8/M11/M13, the T226 line and the coordinator's brief are not in the bundle and are not the GM's words. The ruling does not rest on them.

decisions.why: Mechanism that makes the triage see the item the owing names; without it the cascade the GM asked for is cleared by a filter that reads only what the pop-up states.

decisions.why: Scopes the cascade to the check that owns the finding: the 2026-11-23 rule 're-reviews scoped to the change'.

decisions.why: The fix is a reference that later regenerates from the tag, which the GM 2026-11-23 rule (labels propagate by regeneration) calls for.

decisions.summary: After T241 and T236, before T242.
decisions.why: Sequencing only; T226 is not performance work and displaces none.

decisions.summary: Red exit records the failure and rules a cannot-be-done claim through make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: Leaves no defect unfixed and does not narrow the task.

decisions.id: T227-1 no wipe on a feature change; a unit's home feature
decisions.summary: handle_locked no longer replaces the check state on a feature switch; every key stays keyed by unit or subject; a unit's count keeps a home (round_home, the feature its first round was counted in, or the state's old feature for a unit counted before the change); its triggers are filed, and its continue/accept read, under that home; an owed record round is held and batched by every feature.
decisions.why: This repairs the tripwire the root CLAUDE.md and 375 FR-010/FR-011 already require: the same check on the same thing reaching its cap dispatches the arbiter, one binding ruling per unit per trigger. Before this fix a feature switch reset the count, so the cap never fired. Choosing a home over reading every feature's log is a design choice, and the reason the plan gives (an old continue must not lift a new cap, and a new trigger must not read as already ruled) protects FR-011's one-ruling-per-trigger. It narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.id: T227-2 first look only for other checks' EDIT text
decisions.summary: A round is uncounted as a first look only when every unread sentence carries another check's EDIT words on that subject and none carries its own, matched sentence by sentence (containment either way). Hand fixes the session made between rounds count as the fix loop.
decisions.why: This makes the code do what the 374 wave 120 / 0190 rule says it does ('text OTHER checks' edits added'). The code tested 'anything not its own', and a span EDIT could never match a whole sentence, so the measured barracks rounds 2 and 3 went uncounted. The fix restores a ruled rule and widens nothing past it.

decisions.id: T227-3 the arbiter bundle's count read under any feature
decisions.summary: arbiter/bundle.rs counted no longer returns 0 when the state's feature differs from the active one; its counter section and rounds line drop 'in this feature'.
decisions.why: A defect fix that follows from T227-1: the bundle the arbiter rules from (375 FR-011) must show the rounds actually counted. Before this, misnumbered named @1 for a unit on round 3.

decisions.summary: The cap refusal reads 'round N of <check> on <subject> passes its cap of C - ...', with 'in this feature' cut.
decisions.why: The message is reworded to match the new behavior and still names make arbiter-bundle, the compliant command. A wording change, not a change of scope.

decisions.summary: The cap constant is unchanged.
decisions.why: 375 FR-010 caps record checks at two rounds, the same as review checks.

decisions.id: T227-6 found and left: the batch rule restarts the count on any origin/main move (filed T248, lands before T22)
decisions.summary: new_cause restarts a unit's count whenever origin/main moves. With several sessions landing, a third round in one batch is rare, so the 0097 record-format case that prompted this task would still not have been held. Deferred to T248 with a reason, its id and its order.
decisions.why: This narrows the task's motivating case: T227 alone would not have caught P7's 0097 cascade. It is still a legitimate deferral. It is a separate defect in a separately ruled rule (c5db336fd3, 2026-10-12, 'count afresh only in a later batch'). Changing that rule is not this task's fix, and it needs its own measured definition of when the subject has moved. Folding it in here would silently overrule a ruled rule. The deferral meets 451 FR-009's form: why it is not fixed here, the filed task id, and its order ('lands before T22'). Nothing in the GM's request asks for it to be fixed in this task rather than in its own. The defect is filed and sequenced, not dropped.

decisions.id: T227-7 found and left: the record bundle's 'Earlier rounds' still lists only this feature's rounds (not filed)
decisions.summary: bundle/earlier.rs (feature 393) shows a reviewer only the active feature's earlier rounds, with rulings read from the active feature. Left as it is and not filed, because it has no effect on the cap and matches 393's contract wording.
decisions.why: Under the defect rule (constitution XIV, the GM 2026-11-19) this is not a wrong outcome for what T227 fixes. The cap, the trigger and the arbiter's bundle (T227-1 and T227-3) now all follow the unit across features. This section is what a record reviewer is shown, and it does what feature 393 specified. Leaving behavior that matches its own contract is not a narrowing. If someone later shows a reviewer reading wrongly because of it, that would be a defect to file then.

decisions.summary: Performance work? no.
decisions.why: The task holds a review round. Its only added cost is one extra arbiter.jsonl read on a capped repeat. Scheduling under 451 FR-013 is unaffected.

decisions.summary: A changed label on a drawing-page item owes the form check of a pop-up that does not reference the item.
decisions.why: Counted as an exception to 'labels ... propagate by regeneration' (GM 2026-11-23), so it was judged per case, starting from presumed illegitimate. (a) Where the pop-up references the item, the exemption above applies and regeneration carries it, which is the rule as written. (b) Where the pop-up does not reference the item, regeneration has nothing to act on, so the rule cannot apply there. The plan also records that the label word is held in the block's prose (items::faults), so a relabel is a claim change under the GM's 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review'. A relabel to GUESS or UNRESEARCHED also gives the pop-up a new duty under the 2026-11-25 rule the GM approved ('UNRESEARCHED a fifth label on the research pages as well as in the claims'). Where a relabel only exposes a gap that already stood (GUESS to UNRESEARCHED on an unreferenced item), the 2026-11-25 rule still applies, because it puts the new label in the claims. The exception does not empty the regeneration rule, which still covers every referenced item.

decisions.summary: Triage rule (D): a labeled figure of the pop-up's own thing that its Guesses tab does not hold is sent on; the plan names it the one exception to 'a gap filled is a completion, not a correction'.
decisions.why: Starting from presumed illegitimate, and testing both pairs. The GM's own words reach both, so this is not inference. P7: the pop-up says rows ran to 300 ft while the map draws none past 145 ft as a GUESS. A reader is misled, which is a factual finding of the kind the 2026-11-23 rules keep cascading ('only factual findings cascade'), not a style gap. P15: a new UNRESEARCHED toe-shoulder-past-corner that hamlet/marsh does not hold. Here the GM's approval of 2026-11-25 ('UNRESEARCHED a fifth label on the research pages as well as in the claims'; 'note it as being something that is unresearched') requires the label to reach the claims, so leaving it out breaks a rule he approved. The 2026-11-24 instruction ('we really are cascading in situations that do call for it') covers both cases. Purpose test: the gap-fill clause was dropped because completion edits fixed no real flaw. A drawn guess that the pop-up never discloses is the flaw the label rules exist to show, so applying the drop here would defeat their purpose. The scope is narrow: only new or relabeled items, and only of the pop-up's own kind ('An item about another kind on the same page is not (D)'). The cited dev/modals.md M8/M11/M13, the T226 line and the coordinator's brief are not in the bundle and are not the GM's words. The ruling does not rest on them.

blocks: ### T227 (page session P7's cascade, 2026-11-24: record-format was dispatched on 0097 four times across features and the counter held 0 rounds; 2026-11-25: modal-form ran three rounds on sheet/barracks in four minutes and `make arbiter-bundle BATCH=1` said no round trigger was owed)

decisions.id: T227-1 no wipe on a feature change; a unit's home feature
decisions.summary: handle_locked no longer replaces the check state on a feature switch; every key stays keyed by unit or subject; a unit's count keeps a home (round_home, the feature its first round was counted in, or the state's old feature for a unit counted before the change); its triggers are filed, and its continue/accept read, under that home; an owed record round is held and batched by every feature.
decisions.why: This repairs the tripwire the root CLAUDE.md and 375 FR-010/FR-011 already require: the same check on the same thing reaching its cap dispatches the arbiter, one binding ruling per unit per trigger. Before this fix a feature switch reset the count, so the cap never fired. Choosing a home over reading every feature's log is a design choice, and the reason the plan gives (an old continue must not lift a new cap, and a new trigger must not read as already ruled) protects FR-011's one-ruling-per-trigger. It narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.id: T227-2 first look only for other checks' EDIT text
decisions.summary: A round is uncounted as a first look only when every unread sentence carries another check's EDIT words on that subject and none carries its own, matched sentence by sentence (containment either way). Hand fixes the session made between rounds count as the fix loop.
decisions.why: This makes the code do what the 374 wave 120 / 0190 rule says it does ('text OTHER checks' edits added'). The code tested 'anything not its own', and a span EDIT could never match a whole sentence, so the measured barracks rounds 2 and 3 went uncounted. The fix restores a ruled rule and widens nothing past it.

decisions.id: T227-3 the arbiter bundle's count read under any feature
decisions.summary: arbiter/bundle.rs counted no longer returns 0 when the state's feature differs from the active one; its counter section and rounds line drop 'in this feature'.
decisions.why: A defect fix that follows from T227-1: the bundle the arbiter rules from (375 FR-011) must show the rounds actually counted. Before this, misnumbered named @1 for a unit on round 3.

decisions.summary: The cap refusal reads 'round N of <check> on <subject> passes its cap of C - ...', with 'in this feature' cut.
decisions.why: The message is reworded to match the new behavior and still names make arbiter-bundle, the compliant command. A wording change, not a change of scope.

decisions.summary: The cap constant is unchanged.
decisions.why: 375 FR-010 caps record checks at two rounds, the same as review checks.

decisions.id: T227-6 found and left: the batch rule restarts the count on any origin/main move (filed T248, lands before T22)
decisions.summary: new_cause restarts a unit's count whenever origin/main moves. With several sessions landing, a third round in one batch is rare, so the 0097 record-format case that prompted this task would still not have been held. Deferred to T248 with a reason, its id and its order.
decisions.why: This narrows the task's motivating case: T227 alone would not have caught P7's 0097 cascade. It is still a legitimate deferral. It is a separate defect in a separately ruled rule (c5db336fd3, 2026-10-12, 'count afresh only in a later batch'). Changing that rule is not this task's fix, and it needs its own measured definition of when the subject has moved. Folding it in here would silently overrule a ruled rule. The deferral meets 451 FR-009's form: why it is not fixed here, the filed task id, and its order ('lands before T22'). Nothing in the GM's request asks for it to be fixed in this task rather than in its own. The defect is filed and sequenced, not dropped.

decisions.id: T227-7 found and left: the record bundle's 'Earlier rounds' still lists only this feature's rounds (not filed)
decisions.summary: bundle/earlier.rs (feature 393) shows a reviewer only the active feature's earlier rounds, with rulings read from the active feature. Left as it is and not filed, because it has no effect on the cap and matches 393's contract wording.
decisions.why: Under the defect rule (constitution XIV, the GM 2026-11-19) this is not a wrong outcome for what T227 fixes. The cap, the trigger and the arbiter's bundle (T227-1 and T227-3) now all follow the unit across features. This section is what a record reviewer is shown, and it does what feature 393 specified. Leaving behavior that matches its own contract is not a narrowing. If someone later shows a reviewer reading wrongly because of it, that would be a defect to file then.

decisions.summary: Performance work? no.
decisions.why: The task holds a review round. Its only added cost is one extra arbiter.jsonl read on a capped repeat. Scheduling under 451 FR-013 is unaffected.
